correctness.rationale: For x nonzero the uniquely normalized duality functional on complex ell_p^n yields sum_i |x_i|^{p-2} conj(x_i) y_i / ||x||_p^p. Since all complex multiples of m in the multivalued part occur, one nonzero pairing forces the full complex plane; otherwise exactly M⊂N_p(D) annihilates those profiles, leaving a continuous compact image of the unit sphere. For p not an even integer, independence of profiles of distinct projective linear forms follows by choosing a point on only one kernel and restricting to a transverse real line: the singled-out signed power t|t|^{p-2} is not analytic while other terms are analytic. The one-dimensional/zero-functional cases are accounted for. At p=2j, the duality profile is a polynomial of bidegree (j−1,j); independence of z^alpha conj(z)^beta gives the exact rank-nullity coefficient test. For the n=2k+1 finite-difference family, order-2k binomial weights annihilate degree≤2k−1 polynomials, hence j≤k; for j>k the finite difference of (1+t)^{2j−1} is strictly positive by the positive 2k-th derivative. With non-even p, projective independence rules out the nonzero multivalued vector. The spectrum remains C for k≥2 as ran(R−λI) lies in D+M of dimension at most 3<n. Independently computed 18 exact finite polynomial-identity/check cases after reading verify_finite_difference.py; they corroborate only finite parameters, not the general proof.
